What is the Alphabet?

The English alphabet is a set of letters used to write every word in the language.
Each letter has a name and one or more sounds.
How many letters does the English alphabet have?

Uppercase and lowercase

Every letter has two forms:
An UPPERCASE form (A, B, C) used at the start of sentences and names, and a lowercase form (a, b, c) used in the rest of the word.
Which is the lowercase form of 'G'?

Vowels and consonants

There are 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U (Y is sometimes a vowel). The other 21 letters are consonants.

English has 26 letters but roughly 40 distinct sounds, because letters combine to make new sounds like 'sh', 'ch' and 'th'.
The word 'alphabet' comes from the first two Greek letters — alpha (α) and beta (β).
